Board Appointment
Oxford, UK - 27 August 2026 -
Oxford BioDynamics Plc
(AIM: OBD)
, the international biotechnology company advancing personalised healthcare through precision clinical diagnostic tests and EpiSwitch® Orion, its cloud-based 3D genomics platform for pharma and biotech partners, today announces
the appointment of Richard Compton, Chief Executive Officer, to the Board as an Executive Director with immediate effect. The appointment follows the Company's announcement of 30 June 2026 regarding Mr Compton's appointment as Chief Executive Officer and the completion of regulatory due diligence by the Company's Nomad.
Iain Ross, Non-Executive
Chairman of Oxford BioDynamics, said:
"I am delighted to welcome Richard to the Board of OBD. In the short time he has been with the Company as CEO he has proven he has the qualities and experience to lead the team to commercial success. With the support of the shareholders I believe he will be able to realise the success for which we have all been striving."
The following disclosures are provided in respect of Richard Alan Compton, aged 56, pursuant to Schedule 2(g) of the AIM Rules for Companies.
Mr Compton holds 300,000,000 ordinary shares in the capital of the Company, representing 2.2% of the Company's ordinary share capital.

About Oxford BioDynamics Plc
Oxford BioDynamics Plc (AIM: OBD) is an international biotechnology company, advancing personalised healthcare through precision clinical diagnostic tests and EpiSwitch Orion, a cloud-based 3D genomics platform that transforms existing datasets into actionable insights for pharma and biotech partners.
Currently OBD has two commercially available products: the EpiSwitch PSE (EpiSwitch Prostate Cancer Detection Test) and EpiSwitch CiRT (Checkpoint Inhibitor Response Test) blood tests. PSE boosts the predictive accuracy of a PSA test from 55% to 94% when testing the presence or absence of prostate cancer. CiRT is a highly accurate (85%) predictive response test to immuno-oncology checkpoint inhibitor treatments.
The tests are based on OBD's proprietary 3D genomic biomarker platform, EpiSwitch, which enables screening, evaluation, validation and monitoring of biomarkers to diagnose patients or determine how individuals might respond to a disease or treatment.
The Company's recently launched proprietary AI predictive platform, EpiSwitch® Orion, makes the Company's knowledgebase and analytical tools available to researchers and partners, allowing them to generate insights into 3D regulatory biology from existing datasets. EpiSwitch Orion is a cloud-based 3D genomics platform that enables pharmaceutical partners to transform standard sequencing data - including legacy whole genome datasets - into actionable discovery insights in hours rather than months. By revealing the genome's 3D architecture, EpiSwitch Orion illuminates the 90-95% of disease-associated variants in non-coding regions that traditional NGS and GWAS approaches cannot decipher, bridging the gap between statistical associations and druggable therapeutic targets. The platform is supported by the world's largest curated 3D genomics knowledgebase, featuring over 1.5 billion data points and 15 million high-confidence genomic connections validated across 18,000+ patient samples in more than 40 diseases - a foundation built over nearly two decades that enables partners to identify targets, build predictive classifier models, and design precision interventions at unprecedented speed.
OBD's clinical smart tests have the potential to be used across a broader range of indications, and new tests are being developed in the areas of oncology, neurology, inflammation, hepatology and animal health.
Since inception, the Company has participated in more than 40 collaborations with pharmaceutical and academic partners, including Pfizer, EMD Serono, Genentech, Roche, Biogen, Mayo Clinic, Massachusetts General Hospital and Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma America, and has been awarded funding through the US Foundation for the National Institutes of Health's Partnership for Accelerating Cancer Therapies programme and the EU-funded HIPPOCRATES consortium in psoriatic arthritis.
The Company's headquarters and UK laboratories are in Oxford, UK. Its US operations and clinical laboratory are in Maryland, USA, along with a reference laboratory in Penang, Malaysia.
OBD is listed on the London Stock Exchange's AIM (LSE: OBD). For more information, please visit the Company's website,

, X (@OxBioDynamics) or LinkedIn.

latest.content:
Today 07:00

13 August 2026
Oxford BioDynamics Plc
("OBD" or the "Company")
Oxford BioDynamics partners with Dubai London Clinics & Hospitals to bring EpiSwitch® PSE to the UAE
Oxford, UK - 13 August 2026
-
Oxford BioDynamics Plc
(AIM: OBD, the Company), the international biotechnology company advancing personalised healthcare through precision clinical diagnostic tests and EpiSwitch® Orion, its cloud-based 3D genomics platform for pharma and biotech partners, announces that it has entered into a partnership agreement with The Dubai London Clinics & Hospitals Group ("DLCH"), one of Dubai's longest-established private healthcare providers. This agreement makes OBD's EpiSwitch PSE prostate cancer test available across DLCH's network of clinics and hospitals across the United Arab Emirates.
Highlights
·
Agreement to offer OBD's EpiSwitch PSE prostate cancer test across
Dubai London Clinics & Hospitals network
·
End-to-end clinical workflow successfully validated between Dubai and OBD's UK laboratory
·
First commercial partnership for EpiSwitch PSE in the Gulf region
Under the agreement, patient blood samples will be collected at DLCH facilities and processed at OBD's laboratory in the UK. The end-to-end clinical workflow has been successfully validated between the two organisations.
The Company and DLCH will work together to support adoption across DLCH's clinician network, including local market development and engagement with regional payers. Test volumes are expected to build over time as these activities commence.
DLCH operates a network of five facilities, including the Australian Council on Healthcare Standard International (ACHS)-accredited Dubai London Hospital in Jumeirah, Dubai.
Further details on the partnership will be announced jointly by OBD and DLCH in due course.
Richard Compton, Chief Executive Officer at Oxford Biodynamics, said:
"We're delighted to be partnering with DLCH to make EpiSwitch PSE available across its facilities in the UAE. This is our first commercial partnership for the test in the Gulf region and an important milestone as we continue to expand internationally. We've already successfully validated the workflow between DLCH and our UK laboratory and look forward to working closely with the team to support adoption among clinicians and build awareness of the benefits our test can provide."
- ENDS -

company_30s.what_they_do: OBD Ltd. develops and sells advanced epigenetic testing kits that help doctors detect prostate cancer and other conditions early. The core product is a blood‑based test that looks at DNA methylation patterns to flag disease before symptoms appear.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The market for early cancer detection is growing fast, especially as governments push for cheaper, non‑invasive screening. OBD’s test is one of the few that can be run on a simple blood draw and offers higher sensitivity than many existing methods, giving it a competitive edge in a space that is still fragmented.
company_30s.current_state: The company is still in the commercialization phase, having recently signed a commercial partnership for its flagship test. It is cash‑burning and heavily diluted, with no revenue yet. The share price sits near zero, reflecting the high risk investors see in a company that hasn’t proven a revenue stream.

rns_narrative: OBD has been busy turning its science into business. Over the last six months the company announced a new CEO, secured a US contract partnership, and landed a commercial agreement for its flagship test. A fundraising round was also disclosed, showing that the firm is actively seeking capital to fuel its expansion.

These moves signal a pivot from pure R&D to a go‑to‑market strategy, suggesting management believes the product can generate sales soon. The repeated focus on partnerships and commercial deals indicates a shift toward monetization.

The pattern of announcements shows a company that is still trying to prove its viability, but the momentum of securing a US contract and a commercial deal hints at an emerging catalyst that could lift the stock if the product reaches the market.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet skepticism with occasional hopeful sparks
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of traders whisper that the US contract and new CEO could finally unlock value, especially if the test hits the NHS pipeline.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Many voices warn that the company is still heavily diluted, has no revenue, and that the recent contracts are small and may not materialise into cash quickly. The lack of a clear launch date fuels doubts.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter has gone from a flurry of cautious optimism in the last month to a more muted, wary tone today. The community is waiting for a clear launch announcement before committing.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat, meaning the public is largely unaware of OBD. This lack of noise is a good sign for a contrarian play because a surprise catalyst could generate a big swing.

near_term_catalysts: A formal launch announcement of the prostate cancer test in a major market (e.g., NHS or a US insurer).
A positive clinical validation result that can be released to the market, giving the product a credibility boost.
An increase in trading volume that spikes above the 20‑day average, indicating institutional buying.
Any regulatory approval or a new partnership that expands the test’s distribution network.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden uptick in daily volume and a price break above the 200‑day moving average. A clear, dated launch date or a new partnership agreement are the most decisive signals.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of capitulation – the price has fallen far below the 52‑week low and volume has been thin. If the company delivers a launch announcement, the mean‑reversion could start immediately. The APEX score suggests a tight compression, so a break above the current resistance could trigger a bounce.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The company is at a deep crash level, and the recent shift toward commercial deals indicates a potential turning point. If the product launches, the share price could climb to levels that are 5–10 times higher than today, giving a 400–1000% upside. The mean‑reversion thesis is strong because the price is already at a floor with no obvious downside beyond the current level.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The biggest risk is that the product never reaches market, or the contracts fail to convert into sales. The company’s heavy dilution and cash burn could force a capital call that further depresses the price. A worst‑case scenario is a complete loss of the equity stake, with the price staying near zero.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: 100% of the current equity (the price is already near zero). Potential gain: 5–10x if the test launches, translating to a 400–1000% upside. The risk/reward ratio is highly skewed in favor of the upside.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a breakout above the current resistance if volume spikes and a launch announcement is made. Allocate a small portion of the portfolio – say 5% of available capital – because the upside is high but the probability is uncertain. Place a stop just below the recent support level to limit loss to the current price.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a clear launch date or a regulatory approval notice. A sustained volume increase over three consecutive days would also signal that smart money is stepping in.
playbook.if_passing: If the company fails to announce a launch or the contracts collapse, consider exiting. Also watch for any signs of delisting or bankruptcy filings – these would be terminal risks.

ai_insights.bottom_line: OBD is a deep‑crashed, contrarian play that could explode if its prostate cancer test finally launches, but it risks staying near zero if the product never reaches market.
